_about: Hand-written node content for the dungeons of data/dungeons/dungeons.json (the CSV import). Everything here is placeholder-grade text and numbers (balance is out of scope). Per dungeon: defaults (deck archetypes, icons, AIs cycled over its battles), boss (deck/hp/icon), foes (node number -> foe name, or an object {name, deck, size, hp, ai, icon, extra}), events / challenges / loot (node number -> content), blurbs, story_keys (node number -> story key `dungeon.<key>.before/.after`, in the zone story file or in `text` below), scenes (node number -> {before, after} cutscene ids). Event/challenge effects are tokens: heal:N damage:N gold:N pay:N lose:N card:ID boon:Name|max_hp=2,atk=1,def=1,start_hp=1 rescue sever. An event may be {ref: id} naming one the dungeon class still builds in code.

5.title: Locker Room of Legends
5.body: Rows of lockers hold the old champions' kit, every strap labelled by weight class. One locker has been left open, as if somebody wanted you to look.
choices: It smells of victory and eucalyptus. You feel sturdier.
Mostly protein bars, but there is a roll of gold in the bottom.
Nobody has sat here in years. Your shoulders thank you.

12.title: The Sauna of Truth
12.text: The steam asks one honest question: how hard do you lead?

7.title: The Corrupted Pantry
7.body: Shelves of glowing, sickly-green food hum softly. A ladle is still stirring a pot that nobody is minding.
choices: It is delicious. It is probably cursed. You feel strong and slightly sticky.
Some of the pantry is still clean.

10.title: R&D Archives
10.body: Blueprints, recipe cards and signed memos fill the cabinets. Every handwritten note signed by the Grand Chef leans the wrong way.
choices: The chef who wrote these has never held a ladle. The impostor is exposed.
Evidence, and a buyer for it.

4.title: Taste Test Lab
4.text: Beakers, spoons and a very small flag: does your deck have the body for the panel?

2.title: Take-a-Number Kiosk
2.body: A small grey machine offers you a ticket. The display above says NOW SERVING 3. Your number is 4,000,213.
choices: You feel seen, and slightly worse.
The machine jams. A handful of coins falls out.

8.title: Form 27-B Office
8.body: Form 27-B requires Form 27-C, which requires a stamp from the office you are standing in. A clerk slides a pen across the counter.
choices: Everything is in order. A boon is granted, and a small tax is levied.
It works! Mostly. Something in the ceiling disapproves.

12.title: The Shredding Room
12.body: Rows of paper shredders chew through the day's denied appeals. A sign reads: SHRED ONE THING, RECEIVE ONE THING.
choices: The shredder hums happily and pays out.
Nothing is left of Number 4,000,213. You feel lighter.

5.title: Waiting Room of Eternity
5.text: Row after row of chairs. Can your deck outwait the line?

7.title: Weeping Compost Pool
7.body: The pool is the colour of a bruise and it is sobbing very quietly. Things float in it that used to be useful.
choices: It tastes of rain and regret. You feel hardier, and a little poisoned.

12.title: The Heart Roots
12.body: Thick, pulsing roots run from every wall into the chamber beyond: the Rotheart's lifelines. You could cut them. It will hurt, her more than you.
choices: The roots shriek and let go. Whatever waits ahead will be weaker for it.
The roots keep pulsing. The Rotheart keeps its strength.

4.title: Strangled Greenhouse
4.text: The vines are choosing who gets through. Can your deck keep its footing?

3.title: Grand Foyer
3.body: A portrait of a smiling ruler fills the wall. The floor is so polished you can see yourself, and he is standing behind you in every reflection.
choices: The smile never changes. Neither, you realise, does anything else here.
Heavier than it looks. Worth more than it should be.

12.title: The Doppelganger's Lab Notes
12.body: A lab table of food notes: a shapeshifter's recipe for becoming a Grand Chef, with an entire page on how to smile like her.
choices: It explains everything, including why the sauce tastes of nothing.
Somebody downstairs will pay for them.

22.title: Garden of Uniform Flowers
22.body: A thousand identical flowers stand in identical rows. You count them twice. One of them is, very slightly, a different shade of yellow.
choices: It tastes of dandelion. It feels like the first honest thing in the castle.
Pick a handful of the rest
They wilt in your hand and leave behind a few coins.

quest.side_s_town.offer: There is a door under the old well that has been locked since before I was born.
I always thought the key was lost. It was not. Somebody hid it in a chest in this very town. Find it, and we will see what the door is for.
quest.side_s_town.active: The key is in a hidden chest somewhere in town. Look in the odd corners.
quest.side_s_town.ready: You found it. The key to the old door. I am too old for stairs, but you are not.
quest.side_s_town.done: Go on, the iron hatch beside the well. What lies under it was the Old Kingdom's, not mine.
quest.side_s_beef.offer: Only the worthy reach the top. Also bring water.
There is a mountain behind the station, and a barbell on top that is older than the regime. If you want to try for it, buy a protein shake and bring it back. I cannot climb on an empty cup.
quest.side_s_beef.active: Water, friend. A protein shake from the stand will do. Do not spill it.
quest.side_s_beef.ready: That is the best water I have ever seen. Thank you.
quest.side_s_beef.done: The way up the Ascent of Mount Swolympus is open. Take the trail behind the station. Mind the thin air.
quest.side_s_gour.offer: Psst. Over here. Have you ever been to a restaurant with no menu?
There is a golden reservation card hidden in the Buffet: 'Seating: 1. Courses: 3. Survival: optional.' Somebody left it in a stash. Find it and I will tell you where to sit.
quest.side_s_gour.active: The card is in one of the hidden stashes. Golden. You will know it.
quest.side_s_gour.ready: That is the card! One seat, three courses, survival optional. How exciting.
quest.side_s_gour.done: The sliding door to Omakase is open. Leave your fate to the chef.
quest.side_s_necro.offer: Number 4,000,212? They are on 3. Can you help?
There is a ghost in the Waiting Room of Eternity clutching a very old ticket. The queue is stuck. Thin out the roaming staff and I will get you in.
quest.side_s_necro.active: Two roaming staff members, processed. The queue will not move on its own.
quest.side_s_necro.ready: Two fewer. The queue is moving! Slightly.
quest.side_s_necro.done: The Waiting Room of Eternity will see you now. Take a number.
quest.side_s_ref.offer: Someone has been eating ALL the compost. Little paw prints. A tiny crown.
Chase off two of the scavengers and the trail will lead you to the alley under the big dumpster.
quest.side_s_ref.active: Two scavengers. The paw prints are fresh.
quest.side_s_ref.ready: The paw prints lead to the big dumpster. I knew it.
quest.side_s_ref.done: Under the tipped-over dumpster there is a gate made of a bicycle wheel. That is the way to the Trash Panda Throne.
npc.kestrel.intro: Quiet. Primm's enforcers walk this road on the hour.
I am Kestrel, scout for the resistance. If you are going into the city, there is an older way in than the gate.
npc.kestrel.return: The road is clear. For now.
quest.side_s_cap.offer: There is an older way into the city. Nobody remembers it. That is the point.
The resistance remembers. Make your way inside and meet Wren in the Crease; she will tell you what the old tunnels are for, and I will show you the hatch.
quest.side_s_cap.active: Find the resistance hideout. Ask Wren about the tunnels.
quest.side_s_cap.ready: You found them. Good. Then you have earned this.
fx.old_tunnels_way_in: The grate beneath the plaza lifts with a groan. Light from the perfect city pours in, and behind you the old tunnels run on: four factions' services, still connected.
You climb up past the walls. Nobody is watching this way in. Nobody remembers it. That is the point.
quest.side_s_cap.done: The hatch at the east end of the Outskirts leads down to the Old Service Tunnels. Mind the patrols.
dungeon.dg_s_beef_boss.before: A stone colossus sits at the summit with its hands out, palms up, as if waiting for a barbell to be placed in them. It has been spotting for a thousand years and it is very, very ready.
"Lift," it rumbles. "I will catch it." It does not say what happens if you fail.
dungeon.dg_s_beef_boss.after: The Ancient Spotter lowers its hands and, for the first time in a thousand years, sets something down. The barbell on the altar is yours.
"Good form," it says. Then, quieter: "Thank you for coming up."
dungeon.dg_s_gour_boss.before: The Itamae Supreme lifts a long knife and does not look up. "There is no menu. You have trusted me with three courses. Now, the Chef's Choice."
Behind him a bull made of toro lowers its horns, politely.
dungeon.dg_s_gour_boss.after: The Itamae bows, wipes his knife on a cloth and slides a small plate across the counter. "Omakase," he says. "I leave the rest to you."
dungeon.dg_s_necro_boss.before: A single desk under a single green lamp, buried in forms. Betty Bones looks up, very slowly, and sighs the sigh of the deceased.
"I am very sorry," she says, "but you will need forms A through F."
dungeon.dg_s_necro_boss.after: Betty stamps one last form with a bony flourish. "Fine. Number 4,000,212 is approved. Do not tell anyone I did this."
Somewhere far down the line, a ghost with a crumpled ticket begins, very quietly, to cheer.
dungeon.dg_s_ref_boss.before: The Throne of Lids creaks. On it sits a very large raccoon in a very small crown, sweating profusely.
"I can explain the compost," His Majesty says, "and I would like to do so after you leave."
dungeon.dg_s_ref_boss.after: The raccoon king abdicates with great dignity and a crust of pizza. The crown rolls under the throne. "The compost," he says, "was for the kingdom."
dungeon.dg_s_cap_boss.before: A metal grate lets in light from a perfect city. Beneath it stands Captain Spotless, polishing his shield with a sleeve he has polished before.
"These tunnels do not exist," he says. "I cannot allow you to have found them."
dungeon.dg_s_cap_boss.after: The Captain sits down on a barrel and, for a moment, looks very tired. "I remember when these tunnels were full of people," he says. "Go on. The grate is not locked."
dungeon.dg_s_town_boss.before: A glowing four-coloured core hums at the heart of the vault. Beside it a clockwork guardian unfolds, with a sound like a very old clock remembering the hour.
"Identify," it says. "The Old Kingdom's banner is not for just anyone."
dungeon.dg_s_town_boss.after: The Automaton clicks, whirs and lowers one knee. In its outstretched hand, folded neatly, is the Old Kingdom's banner.
"Four Paths," it says. "One kingdom. Carry it well."
